data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word ‘enosh’ meaning 'man' or 'mortal'. In the Bible, Enos was the name of the son of Seth and the second person to be born after Adam and Eve. The name Enos carries the meaning “Man; mortal” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Enos usually hope their child will grow to embody man; mortal and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: ענוס
in_hebrew.meaning: ענוס הוא שם שפירושו חזק, יציב, או מתמיד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ענוס נגזר מהמילה העברית 'ענוס', שפירושו חזק, יציב, או מתמיד. הוא מופיע בתנ'ך בספר בראשית כאחד משמותיו של האדם הראשון, אנוש בן שית, שחי אחרי הולדת אדם. השם ענוס משמש גם כחלק מהמסורת היהודית והנוצרית כאחד, ומבטא את הרעיון של יציבות וחוזק רוחני.

in_greek.name: Ἠνώς
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Ἠνώς προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑβραϊκὴ λέξη 'ענוס', ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει ισχυρός ἤ σταθερός. Στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, ὁ Ἠνώς ἀναφέρεται ὡς ἕνας ἀπὸ τοὺς ἀπόγονος τοῦ Αδάμ. Ἡ σημασία τοῦ ονόματος Ἠνώς εἰς τὴν παράδοσιν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας εἰς τὴν ἀνθεκτικότητα καὶ πνευματικὴν δύναμιν.

in_latin.name: Enos
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Enos derivatur a voce hebraica 'ענוס', quae significat robustus vel stabilis. In Scriptura Sacra, Enos apparet ut unus e posteris Adae. Nomen hoc in traditione christiana vim spiritualem et stabilitatem exprimit.

in_english.name: Enos
in_english.long_meaning: The name Enos originates from the Hebrew word 'ענוס' (Enos), meaning strong, steadfast, or permanent. It appears in the Bible in the book of Genesis as Enosh, son of Seth. The name carries significant spiritual meaning in Christian tradition, symbolizing strength, stability, and endurance. Historically, Enos has been used across various Christian cultures, reflecting its biblical roots and the virtues it represents.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Enos" holds significance in Jewish and Christian cultures, especially in relation to the biblical figure of the same name. Enos is mentioned in the Book of Genesis as a benefactor and successor to his father Seth, and the third generation ADAM (from Adam). His name signifies the beginning of human population growth after Adam and Eve. He is described in Genesis 4:25-26 as a man who 'begat, and then died: for he (Enos) called upon the name of the LORD'. Thus, the cultural impact of the name "Enos" is an emphasis on human history and the important role of faith and prayer in the face of mortality.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Enos" also holds deep spiritual significance, as it serves as a reminder of the human condition and our connection to God. In Jewish and Christian traditions, the name "Enos" is associated with the concept of the 'mortal man' and the transient nature of human existence. Prayer and devotion to God are seen as essential practices for managing the fear and uncertainty that accompany our mortality, a realization that stems from the character's name. Therefore, the spiritual significance is a testament to the importance of faith, divine connection, and personal reflection, honoring the legacy of the father and ancestor, Enos.
